questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures and new country, sunny city, nice reputation of university. And I have heard so much great about Lisbon, I knew so many that recommended the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of the best decisions I have my made in my life. It was an absolutely amazing and perfect experience despite covid. I met so many nice people and I explored most of Portugal. Lisbon has such a nice vibe, it is a capital but still kind of small and charming.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, both the guidance office of Copenhagen and Nova School of Business and Economics were very helpful. The answered all my questions. KU also invited me to a webinar about studying abroad.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of mails, a lot of webinars and a lot of orientation and introductions at school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The mobility office at Nova SBE would reply in a couple of hours - so helpful!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through facebook. I joined a erasmus group on facebook! I would really recommend that. I found to other roommates that had the same wishes to an apartment. We found a big apartment in the city center to a cheap price. But join the "Erasmus Life Lisboa" groups or similar to the city you are going to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me, I would never choose on campus. Nova SBE is an hour away from the Lisbon city center, so if you want to do something spontaneous you need to travel a lot doing the weekends etc. And the city of Nova SBE, Carcavelos, is kind of boring doing the nights and weekends. But if you want to live close to the university and beach and enjoy a silent atmosphere, I would choose on-campus. But on-campus is really expensive. If you want to live off-campus as I did, I would recommend you to live close to Cais do Sodré (the main station in Lisbon).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Well, I did not use the housing to students so I don't know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, all registration was on a website. And when I had fill in some more, the mobility team would send me emails regarding registration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As mentioned before, on a website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: For me, it was not necessary to ask for help regarding the registration, it was really easy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted! So very successful!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check all your emails! You can find all the information there. But if you still have trouble, just send an email to the mobility team.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was not the highest compared to in Copenhagen, but that suited me well! Then I had more time with my friends and time to explore the country.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not that high, a lot of information and not much math as in Copenhagen. Though, introduction to programming was difficult but it was easy to pass the course, because the grade was mostly based on hand-in-assignments. But courses like business history and development economics were kind of easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from University of Copenhagen! A lot of group work, a lot of presentations and a lot of assignments. More workloade during the semester, but in the end the final exam was easier to pass. Also some of the courses had attendance and participation. For example, in development economics 50% of the grade were based on the final exam, 15% of the grade were based on a presentation, 30% were based on an assignment and lastly, 5% were based on participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Programming
Development Economics
Business History
Advanced Microeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Development economics was really interesting. Business history was relevant but a bit boring. Introduction to Programming was difficult but really fun! I only chose advanced microeconomics because it was a mandatory course at University of Copenhagen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot - for instance to the Azores, and that was of course an unexpected course but worth it! Then I just spent a lot of money on food, clothes, surf trips etc. But of course everything was cheap, but when you buy a lot of everything it just costs a lot of money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are cheap! You can get two beers and one shot for 2 euros! Sports were also cheap, I had private tennis lessons 4 times a month for only 35 euros (really cheap compared to Denmark). Housing was cheap as well (if you do not get scammed, as I have heard from other).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nova SBE encourages you a lot to join clubs, sports etc. They had surf clubs, women's clubs etc. I did not join any club but I joined some of the events!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sunset events where you drink beer and enjoy each others company. I guess if it was not for covid, more events would occur. I joined some surf trips with the school.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf club, NovAfrica. But again, I did not join any but they seemed cool!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See some of Portugal, visit Algarve, Porto etc. Go to Bairro Alto, go to K-Urban-Beach Club (bonus info: Portugeuse people go to clubs at 3 am to 7 am....). Go to some Erasmus events. Do not spend all your time reading books about microeconomics, spend your time with friends!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Portuguese people are really good at English, so language barrier was not a problem. Also, the local people are so nice and chill, maybe too chill.. You need to know about Portuguese time, the locals always show up late. You need to learn how to get patient.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you go to a bar or club, you will always end up talking to some locals. But at school, it is a bit difficult to interact with the locals. You spend most of the time with other internationals. Maybe if you join some clubs or the student union you could get to know the locals. When I was on some surf trips with the student union, I got to know some Portuguese students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Portuguese time... Everything is just slow. And they are not as remote as in Denmark. Even to get the transportation card, you need to fill in thousand of things on paper and wait hours in a queue to collect you transportation card.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals are so nice and openhearted. The people just enjoy life and they do not seem stressed at all compared to danish people. I felt safe all the time in the city, even though I lived in the city center, I never felt unsafe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Do not hold back, do all the things you want and do not pay all your attention to school. 2. Get as many friends as you can, so you always have people around you. 3. Live in the city center of Lisbon and not Carcavelos.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is summer until late october/beginning of november. I mean 25-30 degrees in late october. The sea water is really cold all year around! It will get cold in the night, so bring a warmer jacket for november and december. But still it can be around 23 degrees in november as well. Do not bring high heels, the streets of Lisbon is awful. Buy a "Erasmus Life Lisboa" card, so you can get discount and join events. Bring pencil, paper, calculator etc. Most of the exams are going to be on paper. Bring swimsuits!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having so many amazing friends! When no one knows each other, it creates a perfect possibility to get friends from across the world. But most of all, I just had so much fun this semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe all the team work and presentations at school, but it was manageable. Though, the best part about exchange is the social life, the greatest challenge could also be the social life. I did not have many days off where I just spend time alone. You were constantly doing something or seeing someone. That takes a lot of energy, though I do not regret all the things I did. But remember to takes some days off, if you are just too exhausted of all the new impressions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
